#4181. Off the AppStore: Strategic stepping up in Nymble 2

Welcome to Off The AppStore, a weekly feature with a twist. Namely, that while these - as with all the games we cover here - are games that you can play on your phone, they're ones that operate outside of the realms of the big two ways to play: The Google Play Store and the Apple AppStore.

That means that there might be a bit of work required in downloading alternative AppStores or  APKs, or that the games can simply be played in your phone browser. We'll make sure to detail that for each game, though. Anyway, read on to find a new game or experience to play Off The AppStore.

Remember fairytales? Of course you do; they comprise over half of all the inspiration for any given piece of media, and there's nothing wrong with that. There's a reason these stories keep getting told, and that's because of how accessible they are. Even with all the fantastical elements that occur in them, they're still pretty easy to follow and learn from. One such tale is that of Jack and the Beanstalk, which teaches you that it's totally okay to steal as long as you go through a botanically provided backdoor and the target happens to be a giant that would eat you if he could. This is the inspiration for Xalezar, who has given us Nymble 2 (giant presence notwithstanding).

While you're never given a name, you fall into the role of a young and adventurous lad just looking to seek glory and fortune, supposedly. He discovers that he has the unique ability to interact with parts of the world by jumping over them. By using his skill, he has learned that certain patches of land will rapidly grow beanstalks leading to the upper levels of the world, which he will happily climb. It's your responsibility to manoeuvre his jumping effectively so that he can make it to the beanstalk safely.

In order to keep climbing, the boy must keep leaping over fertile beanstalk soil. The challenge is that said patches of land are located in isolated areas that can invite all sorts of danger. Luckily, there are plenty of bountiful treasure chests to find in these lands that the boy can open with his jumping powers. Unfortunately, there are also hostile creatures that will be hunting the boy as he moves around the land. As long as he can get the jump on them, he'll live to make it to the beanstalk and get a few gold stars to boot.

Nymble 2 is the second instalment in the 2D puzzle-adventure series about a boy moving up in the world via jumping and magic plants. It's cute, quick, challenging, and a fun little way to keep your mind active while hanging out wherever you are. The more you climb, the more pieces come into play, and the more you'll have to direct your steps and your jumps. The boy has the power of youthful adventure, but sooner or later, he will have to grow up.

Nymble 2 is available to download and play from its itch.io page!

#4180. Award-Winning Composer And Musician Jon Batiste Talks Ocarina Of Time's Music And Why 'Guile's Theme' Goes With Everything

Jon Batiste has collaborated with the likes of Alicia Keys, Lenny Kravitz, Prince, Stevie Wonder, Willie Nelson, and many more. He performed the national anthem at Super Bowl LIX. He's headed up the musical efforts of The Late Show with Stephen Colbert. He's taken home more awards than we can realistically list in this article (including eight Grammys, as well as an Academy Award, a BAFTA Award, and a Golden Globe). But as I sit down with Batiste for a brief conversation about video game music, his energy transcends the Zoom call.

Before I can even ask a question, Batiste begins singing to greet me, then nerds out about my NBA Jam and Street Fighter II cabinets. He begins humming the menu music from NBA Jam and reminiscing about all the quarters he pumped into his local Street Fighter cabinet. The Louisiana native and Juilliard School alum has been an ardent gaming enthusiast for nearly three decades, with compositions from games like Sonic the Hedgehog and Final Fantasy VII inspiring his earliest musical endeavors. Spend enough time watching video game music performances on social media, and you'll likely soon find videos of Batiste sitting with famed Final Fantasy composer Nobuo Uematsu, or of Batiste performing gaming music.

With The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time delivering some of the most iconic music of all time (and Batiste famously loving the music), it makes sense that Nintendo would bring him out to New York to serve as a special guest at the launch event for the Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time remake on Switch 2. I sat down with Batiste for a few minutes to chat about his love of video game music, his history with Nintendo, and why "Guile's Theme" from Street Fighter II just goes so well with everything.

Ocarina of Time is easily one of the most important video games ever made, and one of the things that makes it so special is the music. What about Ocarina of Time sticks out to you sonically?First off, if you want to get super inside baseball, technical music nerdery, which I love to do, in the compositions, there's a way that major chords and minor chords in... no sevenths, just root, third, fifth. They alternate, and it creates this magic that is, like, it's wistful, and it's simple. It feels ancient, and it feels like it's the music that is going on in your mind as you're generating thoughts and your imagination is churning. And the major chords are happening just after the minors in this contrary motion that's happening, so it feels like the music is going like this: It's going up – major, minor – like [sings the main Legend of Zelda theme song].

So, it's expanding and contracting, which is a musical allegory for the expansion and the openness of the world that Link is in. It's like [Koji Kondo] figured out how to capture the essence of the gameplay, but also the essence of magic and simplicity, which I think is really what makes... that's the music's power! So, you could listen to the music in the game, and you could also listen to it apart from the game and experience that magic.

Are there any tracks in Ocarina of Time that stand out to you as the most musically sophisticated or compositionally impressive?Oh man. Well, I think of it as a suite, so that's what makes it actually... there's nothing that's more or less complex, but the thought to figure out how to make all of the themes be interrelated yet singular. "Song of Storms" is, like, for me, that's a personal favorite. That's why I like to play it. I like to play a lot of the themes. That's how I grew up! I would play the game, and then, I would go to an instrument. Once we played for hours on Nintendo, we'd go and play Nintendo on piano! It was like a trade-off there, you know? I've been doing this since I was about 11 years old.

Taking it back to that 11-year-old Jon, talk to me a little bit about your history in general.Okay, so my history with Nintendo goes back to the NES. Christmas morning. Duck Hunt. You remember that? Maybe the first game I ever played. No, the first game I ever played was Donkey Kong, and then Duck Hunt, and then Super Mario Bros. Staples! We're talking about the early '90s. We had a room where I would go – it was my domain – and we had this blue shag carpet, and I would sit back there, and I would basically disappear into the carpet playing Nintendo for hours and hours.

And my mind is kind of... my mind can become a spiral; it can become a tornado. And I realized even then that going into this world of the game, even if I didn't win – it's not about winning or losing – it helps to organize the spiral of my mind and give me ideas and inspiration. So then, I started to get into Street Fighter II when I started to play more communally with my sister and my cousins. Yoko Shimomura, who I also had the pleasure of meeting and collaborating with, she composed incredible themes for each character, and that's when I really started to get a true love for fighting games.

And then, we would play so many of the Street Fighter franchise. We would play a lot of Final Fight. There were so many things... there was Double Dragon, then we got Mega Man... all these different series. Mega Man X is [an] all-time favorite. And then, here comes The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, and that sort of expands the canon while also blending all of the elements: score, combat, the sort of linear quality of, like, a Donkey Kong or Super Mario World, and expanding the world in that way, expanding the canon in that way. Mind-blowing! So,  that sort of solidified my palate in terms of my favorite type of game.

You mentioned Street Fighter II. There's a meme about "Guile's Theme" and how it goes with everything. What about that composition makes it so it has the ability to enhance whatever video you pair it with?Wow! So, it has momentum in a way that is extremely [sings the melody of "Guile's Theme"] ... It draws you in, which is what you want [with] anything that you're starting when you're commencing a journey or watching something. You want it to draw you in, and that kind of pulls you in as that call and response. But it's an immediate announcement with the brass, and then the bass call and response. So, it's automatically giving you this feeling that something's happening, and I've got to pay attention to it! So that's the first step right there. And the tempo is really... it's a great tempo! It almost has the feeling of the great themes from, like, an '80s protagonist that's in a fighting movie. I think that was kind of the archetype. Yoko was probably drawing from that archetype, right? The action-hero archetype.

#4179. Minecraft Is Getting Joy-Con Mouse Controls On Switch 2 In A Future Update

You can try them out now in the closed beta

If you've read our Minecraft Switch 2 review here on Nintendo Life, you'll know one thing currently missing from this version is mouse mode.

Fortunately, an update is already in the works to add Joy-Con 2 mouse controls to this version of the game. These controls can be accessed right now in the closed beta build.

This includes the ability to use mouse controls with either the left or right Joy-Con, and you can also customise settings, such as cursor and camera sensitivity. Additionally, you place blocks with the 'ZL' button, and break and select blocks with the 'ZR' button. Button layout can also be adjusted in the game's settings.

At the moment, there's no release date for the official rollout of mouse controls on Switch 2, but they'll be made available to every player at some point in the future.

In case you missed it, Minecraft players who own a digital Switch copy of the game can currently get a free Switch 2 upgrade until the end of January 2027. Owners of a physical copy on Switch can also get a discount on the Minecraft 'Ultimate Collection' upgrade for Switch 2.

#4177. KFC is Inviting You to a Funeral so You Can Play GTA 6

Daniel is a lifelong gamer with a love for various genres and gameplay styles who enjoys exploring games and playing from various angles.

There are only two days left until the landmark launch of Grand Theft Auto 6, which promises to be immensely profitable for Take Two. The gears of society are already starting to grind to a halt as the world braces itself for a statistically-significant portion of the population to disappear into their homes for an indeterminate period. There’s probably going to be at least one guy in a small town out there somewhere who thinks he’s become the last man alive when he doesn’t see anyone on the streets.

It’s kind of an open secret that everyone who plans to play GTA6 will be ditching work or school on the 19th. Many workplaces around the world are aware of this, and some have even done the sporting thing and given their employees an unofficial holiday for a couple of days rather than trying to work without them. Unfortunately, not everyone has managed to secure an iron-clad excuse, but that’s where a certain purveyor of chicken is stepping in.

On the official Instagram account for the Australian arm of fast food chain KFC, it was announced that everyone’s totally real best friend “Ann Alibi” has tragically passed away, and by sheer coincidence, her funeral will be held on November 19. This isn’t just a marketing stunt; an actual funeral will be held, coincidentally providing the perfect out for anyone in need of a day off.

Arion Kurtaj has pleaded guilty to the 2022 Rockstar Games hack that leaked Grand Theft Auto 6 footage and source code.

The post on the KFC Australia Instagram features a photo invite memorializing the passing of “Ann Alibi,” with an invite reading, “It is with heavy hearts, and a much lighter workload, that we announce Ann finally got her wings. She was always there for us when we needed her, in sickness, and in perfect health. By remarkable coincidence, her service will take place on the very same day something thirteen years in the making finally arrives.”

The invite adds that a service will be held from 11:00 AM, and urges attendees to “please let your manager know.”

By remarkable coincidence, her service will take place on the very same day something thirteen years in the making finally arrives.

The real-life funeral will be held at KFC’s Robina, Queensland location, and will include “a hearse, coffin, floral tributes, a book of condolences, an order of service and even a heartfelt eulogy delivered by a surprise guest."

Anyone who attends the service in person will be treated to some complementary chicken, but for everyone who can’t be there for, y’know, whatever reason, will be able to livestream the event online. Plus, KFC’s Australia locations will be offering free delivery all day on the 19th.

KFC is offering just about every semi-realistic avenue for turning this obviously-fake funeral into a genuine excuse for a day off, with the aforementioned book of condolences being the perfect way to create a paper trail for those in need of an excuse for a day off.

"We appreciate that Australians have responsibilities, but some occasions are simply too important to miss," a KFC Australia spokesperson said in a statement obtained by Australian business outlet Human Resources Director. "And in accordance with Ann's final wishes, we've made sure the funeral takes place during working hours."

Surveys suggest that around 12 million Americans are planning on either adjusting work schedules or taking PTO, though given the sheer size of this launch and its accompanying social movement, it wouldn’t be especially surprising if many players didn’t even bother to concoct an excuse.

Some workplaces know that trying to corral employees away from GTA6 would be a foolhardy endeavor, and as such, aren’t even bothering. Palworld developer Pocketpair recently announced that all of its employees are getting time off from Thursday to Monday, just to keep friction to an absolute minimum.

GTA VI will be one of the biggest video game releases in our lifetimes, and it will be talked about for years to come.

#4176. The Video Games And More You Should Play This Weekend – November 6, 2026

This week and weekend is all about the remake of The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time, one of the few games I feel deserves the title of masterpiece. And the remake is really well done! I got every heart piece, every Gold Skulltala, the Goron Sword, and the biggest pouch for every one of my items over the course of the review... but I am contemplating jumping right back in for another go.

We also revealed our next cover and in case you missed the announcement it is... pause for effect... Tomb Raider: Legacy of Atlantis! It's an awesome cover that celebrates the history of Lara Croft, and along with a cover story on the game, we also have a big retrospective on the series. I highly recommend subscribing to get your issue if you haven't already.

But it wasn't all just Zelda and Tomb Raider this week. Below you will find a list of weekend play recommendations, but before that... some of our biggest stories of the week.

We have been writing a lot about The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time remake this week because it is one of 2026's most exciting games, and it's real good. The remake is not particularly surprising. It mostly sticks to the trajectory of the original game, but there is a reason it is considered one of the best games of all time. It also looks and plays amazing.

You can read the full review here (or watch the video above), but we also have a big interview with the game's producers (one of whom worked on the original Ocarina of Time, and one who directed Breath of the Wild among many other Zelda games), some details about the Easter Eggs that did and did not make it into the remake, and a very handy tip for the game if you happen to be playing with a Switch 2 Pro controller.

World of Warcraft: Forever is out now and it’s a great time to jump into the revamped and expanded version of a project that changed online games forever back in 2004. A thousand new quests, multiple new zones, countless revamps, and an impressively stunning visual overhaul make it the perfect time to jump in for anyone who’s ever been curious to explore Azeroth.

2022's Escape Academy was a sneaky little puzzle game that surprised me and its sequel released this week. Taking place in a school obsessed with puzzles, you play as a student who must make their way through a series of escape rooms. The puzzles are clever, and the setting is charming, but the secret weapon is the local, split-screen co-op. Solving puzzles together is fun especially when one player needs to look at one section of a room to help dictate a solution on the other side of the room. My wife and I both love video games, but rarely play co-op games together just because of our disparate, individual tastes. But Escape Room is one we enjoyed together and we're so far enjoying the sequel. My only complaint so far is... I wish it ran a little better.

While we collectively use the term here for the sake of familiarity, I’m always a bit hesitant in my own mind to label a game under the wide banner of “Metroidvania.” In part, that’s because I think the two referenced games (Metroid and Castlevania: Symphony of the Night) are actually more different than they might appear at first glance. Gloomsoft’s recent release, Moadra, recognizes that distinction, crafting a game that draws heavy inspiration from the specific tradition of Super Metroid, even while presenting an intriguing and atmospheric fiction that is great fun to discover. In movement, actions, and exploration, Moadra feels remarkably similar to  the best of the 2D Metroid games. A scanning tool also leans into the Metroid inspirations, revealing details about the weird alien world you’re navigating. If you’ve been hungry for a game that scratches that particular itch of sci-fi gear/ability-gated exploration, I think you’ll find a lot to love in this game.

I get the Marvel fatigue we've all been experiencing. There are a lot of games and a lot of movies and a lot of TV shows and many are good, but lately most feel like homework. For those reasons, you'd be forgiven for dismissing the 2021 Guardians of the Galaxy game, but I promise you it is good. For one, it is standalone. It does not directly tie to any specific Marvel media. No homework necessary. And for two, it's just a really good game with an affecting story and a unique take on the characters that most of us met for the first time in the movies. And, for the BioWare fans out there mourning the loss of Mass Effect, this game has some Mass Effect energy. It's available on Switch 2 this week and I happily recommend it, especially if you missed it five years ago.

This exclusively two-player board game features a fun mix of activities. You act as both a dungeon architect, and an adventurer delving into said dungeons. Each player creates their own version of a challenging dungeon filled with traps, monsters, and treasures.

But you’re also forced to take on the dangers of your opponent’s crafted dungeon, to see who manages to come out on top. If you have fond memories of the hidden-info nature of old games like Battleship, but you want some greater strategic depth and fantasy flavor thrown in, this one is a great pick.

#4175. After 15 years, The Sims' best spin-off finally gets its due follow-up in The Sims 4: Royalty & Legacy

The Sims Medieval had a short but powerful run back in 2011, and now many of its best features are finally coming to the main franchise.

The Sims 4 developers recently promised an exciting year for the game, and the franchise as a whole, and we just got an early look at one of those first events. After some light teasing, the developer unveiled Royalty & Legacy, the game’s next expansion.

Royalty & Legacy’s first trailer debuted on Thursday, revealing a February 12 release date, and showing off the expansion for the first time.

There’s a lot going on in Royalty & Legacy, which is priced $40. For one, it introduces a new world, Ondarion, which is going to be the setting for your kingdom, as you join a race for the throne. The expansion introduces Dynasty and Nobility - two new systems you can use to create your own world of royal shenanigans.

Ondarion is made up of three neighborhoods (regions). Each region has a unique theme and culture, and they’re each ruled by a Dynasty. Dambele is a place that prioritises art and community. Verdemar is a chaotic world of outlaws and nobles. Finally, Bellacorde is an extravagant region known for opulence and romance.

Speaking of building places, Royalty & Legacy also adds a new Lot type, The Backroom Lot. It serves two functions that change with the time of day. For instance, it can be a library or gym in the morning, and shift into a night club at night. Dambele has its own library-turned-rave, for instance.

At the heart of Ondarion are all the possible fantasy lives and stories you can live. The Sims calls them Powershifts, and they include some well-known Arthurian fantasies and other, more silly ones.

Swordsmanship is the new 10-level skill arriving with the expansion, which further plays into those fantasies by letting your Sims duel. There are even Swordsmanship Tournaments you can watch take place across every neighborhood in Ondarion.

Then there are Secret Passageways, which let you speed up moving across the new regions. They essentially let your Sims teleport between designated passageways, either on their own lots, or other lots in the world. Some of these are hidden for you to find, while others you can create.

In terms of new careers, there’s the Noble Career, where your Sim can rise through several Noble Rankings by doing basically what nobles had to do in the middle ages to earn favour.

The aforementioned Dynasty System is how you can join any of Ondarion’s existing families, or start your own. You actually have a lot of say in what goes on, including the usual business of appointing heirs.

Of course, no royal roleplay would be complete without scandals, which is where the Scandals System comes in. Through it, you can create stories to discredit others, or even topple an entire dynasty.

In November, you may recall The Sims 4 introducing new free items inspired by West African culture. In creating that content, EA worked with a group of Simmers who have direct ties to West African countries.

The group’s guidance was once again utilised to build the Dambele neighborhood in this expansion, and some of the lots around the world of Ondarion were even created by members of the group.

While you wait for Royalty & Legacy to actually arrive, there’s more in The Sims 4 you can jump in right now. The game recently kicked off a collaboration with fashion brand Coach that brought several free items to Create a Sim, and Build Buy. That arrived alongside a free update, which already makes for a busy start of the year for The Sims 4.

#4174. 35 million of you have already pre-registered for Arknights: Endfield

Ahead of its official release next week, Arknights: Endfield has already surpassed 35 million pre-registrations from players around the world.

Arknights: Endfield developer Gryphline has a good reason to celebrate, as the upcoming free-to-play action RPG has achieved yet another milestone. The developer announced today that Endfield already has over 35 million pre-registrations.

This a major moment for the game, which is poised to be one of 2026’s biggest releases on mobile.

In December, when Gryphline officially revealed the Arknights: Endfield release date, the developer said at the time that the game had surpassed 30 million pre-registrations, meaning over 5 million more have joined in since then.

Arknights: Endfield has pretty much wrapped up closed testing, and we’re in the final stretch ahead of the January 22 launch, when the free-to-play game will go live across PC (where it'll be available via the Epic Games Store, as well as Gryphline's own launcher), PS5, and mobile platforms (iOS, Android).

The developer hosted a livestream to celebrate, where it also debuted two new trailers: the launch trailer (below), as well as another look at gameplay. The gameplay trailer also shows off more of the game’s Talos-2 world, and sets up the mystery at the centre of its narrative.

If you’re going to be playing Endfield on PC, you’ll be happy to know that you can expert a breezy experience with support for 120fps. The game also comes with a wide range of modern technologies, including Nvidia DLSS Super Resolution, and Frame Generation. Both Xbox and PlayStation controllers are supported, too.

You can expect more Arknights: Endfield coverage from us at release and beyond. In fact, based on what we played so far, we’re pretty confident in this early Arknights Endfield characters list.

#4173. Casetify Death Stranding Collection review - "Functional and well designed"

I have been a big fan of Casetify for my entire adult life. I do feel that their cases are just fantastic, and when they announced their collab with Death Stranding 2, the action-adventure game by the legendary Kojima Productions, I was excited to see their designs!

The KOJIMA PRODUCTIONS x CASETiFY collection does have a bunch of different designs, including little plushies! It's quite fun to see these different takes on the video game. I had a look at the DS2 - DHC Magellan Set, which has three different aspects to the set itself.

The first aspect is the phone case. This phone case is sleek - black and grey, with slight designs on it. It's not in-your-face Death Stranding 2, but it's one of those if you know and are a fan, you know. I have had several compliments for this case, especially at gaming events, which is always nice. There is a small double-hole bit on one side, perfect for phone charms if that's your thing. The case is a MagSafe case, so you can use the magnet on the back of it to attach any other MagSafe products to it. Casetify cases are high-impact, so there is no need to worry about dropping your phone, and I feel that my phone has always lasted in these.

Speaking of the MagSafe case, this set came with the Snappy Grip Stand MagSafe Compatible backing, which easily snaps into place using the magnet. I like the pop of colour this adds, though it does cover some of the design on the back of the case. Unlike PopSockets, which can be quite bulky, it sort of folds flat. Popping it up and placing my fingers into it feels very comfortable to hold. I did find that it's not really for constant use (or it might have been my batch), as when it was in my pocket it got a little warm and felt sticky on the edges from the glue holding it together.

The third item within the DS2 - DHV Magellan Set is the AirPods Pro 3 Impact Case, which is a two-part protective case which fits well over the top of your AirPods. The clip itself is very durable, with the Casetify logo on it, and doesn't feel like it would fall apart or anything. It's simple, but well designed.

I have always been a fan of Casetify and very much like these collabs! These make great gifts for gamers and are also extremely functional as well.

Zelda Notes might not appeal to everyone, but in the Ocarina of Time remake on Switch 2, Nintendo is using it to track global player data.

If you haven't already taken a look, roughly a week after the launch of this title, there are now some rather interesting player stats. This includes information about the top "game over causes", the types of special items used, and much more.

As you can see, players (18%) are most commonly "falling victim" to ReDead. Some other stats reveal the Hookshot as the most used special item, and the top damage sources are traps.

Here's a quick rundown of the current global play data after a week:

Some additional stats shared on the app reveal the average clear time is around the '20 hours+' mark. Again, you can get a more detailed rundown about all of the global play data on the Zelda Notes app. Keep in mind this data will change over time as more people play through the title.

#4170. Petit Planet Hands-On Preview – Creature Comforts

Petit Planet marks Hoyoverse’s maiden voyage into the life sim genre popularized by games like Animal Crossing, Stardew Valley, and, most recently, Pokémon Pokopia. The creators of Genshin Impact, Honkai: Star Rail, and Zenless Zone Zero have crafted well-received, lucrative free-to-play gacha games across several disparate genres; Petit Planet, fittingly, sees it try to attract yet another world of players. It’s been a year since I first played Petit Planet’s initial alpha test, and I spent a couple of more hours exploring its cozy cosmos at the Hoyoverse Media Tour in Seoul, South Korea. Although what I played has not dramatically changed my opinion of the game – it remains a delightful, if familiar, good time – speaking to its lead designer who goes by the single name Murphy and lead artist Yunli Huang helped shed light on how Petit Planet will differentiate itself from contemporaries and its approach to multiplayer, storytelling, and monetization.

The game’s premise centers on a customizable protagonist who sets out to populate their own personal planet (which is about the size of King Kai’s world from Dragon Ball Z). Although you are ostensibly human, everyone else is a talking animal. Your mentor of sorts is a chillax sheepdog named Mobai, who enjoys wearing straw hats and dropping his catchphrase/life mantra “Mo worries” and “Mo Rush.” The business-minded Glenn the Squirrel is a shopkeeper and seems like a cuter, less aggressive Tom Nook. Yunghou is a shy fox who enjoys farming and has the slightest hint of a southern accent. These critters and many more inhabit your planet, which you’ll grow from an empty (but vibrant) rock into a bustling village filled with homes, businesses, crops, decor, and, of course, neighbors.

Story is rarely a hook for a genre that largely promotes creating your own fun through the emergent moments with your neighbors and friends in multiplayer. Still, after Pokémon Pokopia presented an unexpectedly wild and fascinating tale, I ask if players should bother getting invested in a grander narrative à la Genshin Impact. The short answer seems to be “not so much.”

“Unlike other Hoyoverse games, there is no such main plot,” Murphy explains in my group interview. “There will be a main story at the beginning, but the main purpose is just to guide the players, get more familiar with the setting and the world. But the whole narrative of this game will be more fragmented. For example, if you look at those descriptions of those items, there will be a lot of content and narrative behind it. If you look at the description of creatures, many of them are real creatures in real world, and you get to learn more knowledge of this creature by reading those descriptions. And also, we've developed a very comprehensive narrative for each of our neighbors, so that is also part of our, called like, main plot, main narrative, because we want to make this world more like more lively and a more livable world. So that is how we treat narrative in this game."

While players who enjoy a substantial story to propel them through a game may be disappointed, those looking to unwind with a laid-back experience should be pleased. Hoyoverse is designing Petit Planet to be a no-pressure experience to enjoy at your leisure, hence why it emphasizes it as a life sim more than a management sim. There are no complicated stats to manage; simple inputs make it easy to pick up and play; imperfection is encouraged, with Hoyoverse comparing the experience to doodling as a child: your creation may not be perfect, but you had fun bringing your imagination to life.

I spent the first hour of my roughly two-and-a-half-hour session starting from scratch to see if any notable changes were made to this introductory portion in the last year. If there are any differences, they’re imperceptible because I wen went through the same onboarding of learning how to catch bugs and fish, building your first home, inviting your first neighbor, and farming crops, all while growing a magical sapling that, after performing enough tasks, blooms into a full tree that brings new life and mechanics to your world as it grows. Performing special tasks for residents, from completing requests to simply interacting with them, grows their bond, which, when high enough, will entice them to move in. For veteran genre fans, it’s a familiar song and dance. What I did notice this time around is how refreshingly quick the onboarding is. You have all of these foundational mechanics within the first 45 to 50 minutes, which is a nice pace. It was a good refresher for some foundational mechanics I’d forgotten since I last played, but it created an appetite to dive deeper.

Thankfully, Hoyoverse provided a second build set many hours into the game to give an idea of how planets can evolve. This build was set during winter, one of Petit Planet’s revolving seasons that alter the environment and introduce themed cosmetics and decor for players and residents. Sporting winter gear, I ran around the snow-covered planet, which was densely populated with shops, homes, and neighbors. I was initially greeted by unfamiliar faces named Trixie and Kookoo, who provided weather forecasts and news reports reminiscent of Isabelle from Animal Crossing and Callie and Marie from Splatoon. My sparse quest log was tricky to tackle since they revolved around mechanics I had no context for, such as setting up Vignettes. These are essentially templates for unique scenes filled out by dropping the correct furniture pieces in their layout; in this case, I had to set up an outdoor movie on the beach.

I only spent roughly an hour with this late build, and my biggest takeaway was simply how dense and lovely the village looked. A lot of work went into crafting this build, which boasted a farm filled with different crops (with unlockable recipes to create dishes from them), crafting tables to build furniture from collectible blueprints, and several shops, including Glenn’s to purchase a revolving selection of decor items. None of what I saw surprised me, however. Petit Planet so far checks many of the boxes you’d expect and want from a life sim. My cursory tour of a later-game planet did little to reveal any big new ideas, but what I did experience seemed perfectly cromulent.

My biggest question regards multiplayer. As much as I enjoy Animal Crossing: New Horizons and Pokémon Pokopia as solo experiences, playing with friends feels like a mean joke because of the tedious number of hoops to jump through just to invite other players into your world. And even once your buddy arrives, interactions are disappointingly limited. When I ask if Petit Planet offers a comparatively frictionless multiplayer experience, Murphy vaguely assures smoother sailing. “The multiplayer experience is a very important part of our game because, just as the interaction with NPCs, the interaction with other players is also a form of building up emotional connection to this game, and we want to provide that kind of experience to our players.” More specifically, Murphy cites features such as dynamic server load adjustments based on player counts and the option to allow or ban visiting players from taking resources from your planet to prevent griefing.

As a free-to-play Hoyoverse game, monetization is a major talking point. In Petit Planet’s case, the team agrees that rolling for neighbors gacha-style would be strange and defeats the spirit of the genre. Instead, all monetization will revolve around cosmetics; players can unlock new furniture and themed decor sets, outfits, and other cosmetic accessories for their character. Unlocking a full themed set of decor earns currency points, and there are myriad reward meters to fill for performing mundane tasks like greeting residents or catching bugs. It remains to be seen if and how Petit Planet’s progression begins nudging players into opening their wallets, but Hoyoverse promises it will be an experience that deemphasizes grinding.

I also briefly checked out the recently announced Switch 2 version of Petit Planet. My impressions after about 15 minutes of playtime: it’s fine. It sometimes ran noticeably hitchier than the PC version I spent most of my time with, but it seems perfectly adequate so far and, hopefully, will be a smooth experience when it launches sometime next year.

Since life sims require more than a couple of hours to fully reveal their quality, it was tough to get a read on Petit Planet even with this new showing. The game looks beautiful thanks to Hoyoverse’s signature sharp and colorful visual style. It has a relaxing vibe, and feels mechanically decent for the most part. In short, it seems broadly fine and like a respectable take on the genre. I suspect its biggest appeal will be that it will receive what Animal Crossing: New Horizons lacked: years of constant, substantial support.

Hoyoverse is very good about keeping fans of its games well fed with regular updates for years on end, and I don’t expect it to stop now. The idea of a seemingly well-made spin on Animal Crossing that’s free to download and, unless it completely bombs, will almost certainly receive years of new content is enticing on paper. I imagine this is the reason Petit Planet is coming to Switch 2 next year, where it can lure in Animal Crossing and Pokopia players before other consoles. PC and mobile players, meanwhile, must only wait until December 4 when Petit Planet fully launches to see if it has the chops to stand alongside the coziest giants of the genre.

#4169. Tomorrow's Battlefield 6 patch somehow makes jets more useless, improves armor bar visibility in Redsec

The first Battlefield 6 patch of the year is almost here, bringing a smattering of changes, including one that doesn't quite make sense.

Battlefield 6’s promised, season-extending update has been officially detailed. The patch, version 1.1.3.5, arrives tomorrow, January 20 right when Season 1 was supposed to end. Part of the update’s goal is to extend the current season, until Season 2 kicks off in the middle of February.

Update 1.1.3.5 does, of course, have a change log of its own that goes beyond just the season’s extension, but the changes fall somewhere between not very exciting, and a bit puzzling.

Patch 1.1.3.5 is, for all intents and purposes, a smaller update. When Battlefield Studios announced it earlier last week, the developer didn’t promise any major changes or fixes, so expectations never got out of hand.

The patch is mainly made up of bug fixes, but it does have three key areas of improvements to gameplay. There’s a big focus on melee combat, how responsive/unresponsive it is with the various melee tools, and how melee behaviour interacts with sprinting and other animations.

The end result should be faster attack speeds for the knife, and clearer wind-up animations for both the knife and the sledgehammer. The timing dictating when melee damage gets credited has also been made more consistent in different environments.

Interestingly, sprint is now only interrupted when the melee attack reaches its target. As it stands, sprinting is only interrupted after the full duration of the animation has been completed, which adds to the that perceived feeling of sluggishness.

The other major, and arguably most confusing is the nerf to jet cannons. The patch is going to make jets far less stronger against other air vehicles, requiring 40% more hits to destroy a target. This is puzzling because jets - and air vehicles in general - are already the least survivable in Battlefield 6.

And, considering how the rest of a jet's arsenal is either situational or nearly ineffective, the cannons were really the one guaranteed way of downing other air vehicles, so long as you manage to land your shots consistently. While the change is wellmeaning, the percentage will likely be reduced in future patches.

Finally, the update makes a few refinements to UI across the game, though mainly aimed at Redsec and modes where players wear armor. Armor bar visibility has been improved, and there’s a fix for the annoying bug that sometimes caused the armor bar to disappear every few seconds.

#4168. Heartopia surprise launches on Steam and shockingly, everyone seems to be happy

Heartopia players didn't actually end up having to wait too long to play the game on Steam, which is certainly not what anyone expected.

Heartopia has officially arrived on Steam, only a little over a week after it launched on iOS and Android. When the game’s release date was announced back in December, developer XD said it was pushing back the Steam release without offering any hints about how long the delay was going to be.

While the game can be played on PC through TapTap, the developer’s own emulator, many had been anticipating the Steam launch. So you can imagine that when the free-to-play life sim game surprisingly showed up on Valve’s platform on Saturday, there were a lot of happy people.

Heartopia’s Steam release has, much like mobile launch, been a success. We do know that the game reached the number one spot across app stores in over 50 countries, and though the Steam numbers may not be as record-breaking, everything is looking pretty good.

The game peaked at a decent 28,815 concurrent players (via SteamDB) on Steam one day after it launched, and considering how sticky it has been with the majority of those players so far - and the fact the launch itself was a surprise - there’s every chance those figures will improve over the course of this week as it picks up momentum.

Steam user reviews have similarly been quite positive, with the overall rating currently sitting at Mostly Positive, based on over 1,400 reviews.

You’re still need either a Google, Facebook, or Apple account to log into the game, same as you would on mobile. The Steam version does support cross-play with other platforms, so you’ll be able to play with your friends on mobile.

We’ve been playing a lot of Heartopia ourselves, and have been updating and expanding our guides. If you’re looking to get started, such as with how to add and play with friends, how to regain Energy, and how to unlock home plots, our guides offer the best place to start.

Once you’re past the initial hump, you’ll probably be looking for where to find things like mushrooms, bugs, fish, and birds, so definitely bookmark those, too. If you simply like free stuff, our Heartopia codes page is a must read before playing.

#4167. Battlefield 6’s first big map in months is coming to Labs soon, but I'm more excited about BF4's Golmud Railway making its way to BF6

As promised, Battlefield Labs is coming back to bring us a preview of some of Battlefield 6’s upcoming Season 2 content.

Battlefield 6’s Season 2 was recently pushed back by a month to give Battlefield Studios time to polish up its content. Now, the developer has revealed how it plans to use some of that time, and the first port of call is Battlefield Labs.

As discussed in the initial delay message, BF Studios wants the community’s involvement earlier and more consistently in the development of future content. This includes Season 2, of course, and a big component of what it’s bringing to the game is headed to Labs.

The first Battlefield Labs session kicking off soon will focus on Contaminated, one of the new maps coming to Battlefield 6 with Season 2. BF Studios says the map falls between Eastwood and Mirak Valley, in terms of size.

The blog post even likened it to Battlefield 1’s St. Quentin Scar, and Battlefield 5’s Arras. Although we’ve yet to actually play it, the size and description do sound really well, especially in a game as starved of big maps as Battlefield 6 currently is.

Another thing BF Studios wants to test is the way ground vehicle gameplay and aerial presence interact with infantry combat, which is pretty standard for most Battlefield maps. Interestingly, there appears to be some sort of mechanic unique to Contaminated that the developer also wants to evaluate.

More Labs sessions are planned, including one that will show off new gameplay tools and vehicles. The AH-6 Little Bird helicopter was specifically namedropped, which makes sense given that it’s going to be part of Season 2’s content.

Battlefield Labs sessions will also extend beyond the biggest-ticket items of maps and vehicles. BF Studios said we should expect tests of upcoming features, like the Aircraft Radar, as part of a list of other air combat updates.

Ground vehicles, and they way the various rockets interact with them, will also be evaluated in a different session, with specific adjustments planned for RPGs and TOWs. And, of course, the work to improve and perfect hit reg remains ongoing, and future tweaks will go through Labs first.

There’s even more exciting news for fans of big maps, as the blog post also confirmed that Battlefield 4’s Golmud Railway is currently in the works, planned to go live in a future season. Golmud Railway will show up early in Labs, and you can expect it to evolve over multiple sessions.

For context, when it does arrive in Battlefield 6, Golmud Railway will be the largest map in the game, which is saying something. Though the map is beloved by vehicle players, it has its issues elsewhere, and BF Studios says it will be looking at all that when it creates the BF6, emphasising that it won’t be a simple port of the BF4 original.

Finally, the post throws a bone to Redsec battle royale players still waiting for a Solo mode. BF Studios continues to test the idea internally, but it’s taking a while. Needless to say, there are so many aspects that need to be considered. Game pace, balance, player survivability, match flow just to name a few.

Redsec BR was built with squads in mind, so that task is extra challenging. Though the developer didn’t say when we can expect Solos to arrive in Labs, players will get a chance to experience it before it enters the live game.

#4166. Fatal Fury: City Of The Wolves Is Adding Laocorn From The Motion Picture

The Fatal Fury movie antagonist returns next week

SNK's expansion of the Fatal Fury: City of the Wolves roster will continue with the release of Laocorn next week on 19th November 2026.

This character, who was the primary antagonist in the 1994 anime movie Fatal Fury: The Motion Picture, is part of the game's paid Season 3 DLC line up, and is voiced by Branden Loera.

"Primary antagonist in the 1994 anime film Fatal Fury: The Motion Picture. Laocorn and his twin sister Sulia are direct descendants of Gaudeamus, a mighty warrior from antiquity. With his ever-loyal Triumvirate in tow, he relentlessly pursues the legendary Armor of Mars—intent on transcending humanity and ascending to godhood.

"When he discovers the armor's final piece is part of the prize for the KOF tournament, he enters the competition himself. But will claiming the armor bring him the power he craves—or a fate beyond his control?"

You can check out the trailer above (note: the YouTube video uses auto-dubbing, which does not reflect the voice acting in the game). SNK has also released a "digest movie" of the motion picture to help set the scene:

"Fatal Fury: The Motion Picture (1994) Determined to stop her brother, Laocorn Gaudeamus, from completing the forbidden Armor of Mars, Sulia Gaudeamus ventures alone to South Town in search of Terry Bogard, the hero she hopes can thwart Laocorn's dark ambitions."

Laocorn joins Rick Strowd, Duck King, Kim Kaphwan and Manjiro Sano & Ken Ryuguji as part of Season 3. In December, SNK is also teaming up with Tekken 8, which will see the arrival of Reina in the game. If you haven't already played City of the Wolves on Switch 2, there's a demo you can check out on the eShop.

#4165. Pikmin Bloom Has Upset Players By Referring To Taiwan As China

Sam Woods is TheGamer’s Senior Reporter. He’s been in games journalism since 2020 and has undertaken a variety of roles in that time. These have included roles such as SEO Editor, Managing Editor at DualShockers, and Global Head of Gaming, and he's also been seen on the BBC. He was promoted to the Senior Reporter position in 2025 following a series of high-quality reports and exclusives for TheGamer.

Since 2020, Sam has written over 3,000 articles and specializes in telling the stories of the people behind the games. He’s interviewed the biggest game directors, some of the industry’s top talents, told the stories of how indie games came to be, and spoken to players about what really makes them tick. He’s also interviewed some of the world’s biggest musical artists to find out how the medium has inspired their work, and TV and Film actors about their roles in video game adaptations. He even hosted a PAX panel in 2021 and made a documentary in 2024 surrounding the creation of a Disney game.

Alongside this, Sam focuses on breaking news. He got the scoop on Perfect Dark’s cancellation, provided context on some AI drama, and revealed that Lady Dimitrescu’s actress would love to step back into the character’s giant shoes. These articles have been picked up by the biggest gaming sites, including IGN, GameSpot, and PC Gamer. He also loves to dive into the numbers behind the games.

Sam’s journey in games journalism has taken him all over the world. He’s covered Gamescom in Germany, Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles, and Tokyo Game Show in Japan, each on three occasions.

He’s been learning Japanese since 2024 with the intention of identifying and translating Japanese-language news and bringing it to English-language audiences first, something he’s done countless times.

Sam’s first review was 2020’s Battletoads reboot, and he’s since reviewed games in The Legend of Zelda, Super Mario, and Pokemon franchises.

Tensions between Taiwan and China are at an all-time high. While the Chinese government, led by Xi Jinping, believes Taiwan is part of China, Taiwan, its government, and its people view the country as an independent, sovereign state. Escalated military drills have taken place over the last year, as outside nations try to calm the issue.

Pikmin Bloom, the mobile Pokemon Go-like Pikmin title, has accidentally waded into the topic by labeling Taiwan as part of China in a recent update, leading to hurt feelings and boycott calls from people in the island nation.

First reported by Taiwanese outlet 4gamers, Pikmin Bloom, a game developed by Scopely, has referred to Taiwan as "Taiwan, China."

An announcement for the game's 5th Anniversary event used the label in the Simplified Chinese version of the release. While 4gamers confirmed that the Traditional Chinese announcement reads "stores throughout Taiwan," the Simplified Chinese version said, "Japan and the Taiwan region of China."

The issue was spotted by Sherry Chou on Threads, who, in their post [translated by Google Translate], said:

"Isn't this game completely unplayable in China? Taiwanese players are still the main source of income, so why are they still trying to curry favor with China? Are the official Pikmin game developers brainless or just used to kneeling? This game is making money off Taiwanese players. As a low-spending player, I can't stand it! If it's not fixed, I'm quitting." The post was dubbed "heartbreaking" by another Pikmin Bloom player.

As a low-spending player, I can't stand it! If it's not fixed, I'm quitting.

Taiwan is currently Pikmin Bloom's biggest market. Spending from the country surged 902 percent in the first half of this year, as the walking/exploration game made $35.7 million, almost as much as it made in all of 2025. $18.5 million of the $35.7 million came from players in Taiwan, with the country taking a 52 percent market share in the first half of the year.

Japan still eclipses Taiwan in lifetime spend, contributing 49 percent of all-time revenue, but Taiwan is closing the gap. This growth in Taiwan has seen collaborations with local Taiwanese brands, including CoCo Fresh Tea & Juice and Family Mart.

It's the second time Pikmin has been involved in controversy in the last few days, with Pikmin 4's Dandori Academy Switch 2 Edition review-bombed and labeled a "scam."

#4164. Arc Raiders finally reveals early 2026 roadmap, but we’re not getting a new map for a while

The first couple of months of 2026 in the world of Arc Raiders look pretty promising, but the big guns are being held back for now.

After weeks of waiting, Arc Raiders developer Embark has officially unveiled the first few months of the game’s 2026 roadmap. The plan is split into four months, covering January to April, collectively dubbed Escalation.

We’re expecting a content update each month, with the majority of the biggest additions happening on the game’s existing maps. There is, however, at least one new map in the works, but it won’t be here until sometime in April.

While we wait for that, Arc Raiders is going to go through several events and other in-game changes, some more meaningful (and exciting) than others. January looks to be the lightest so far, which makes sense given that it’s just a week or so from ending.

January’s chapter is titled Headwinds, kicking off on January 27. This segment will see the addition of a new matchmaking option for players above level 40 - at or near the game’s endgame. We’re also expecting a new Map Condition, and a new Player Project for everyone to contribute to.

Things start getting interesting in February, when Shrouded Sky will begin. This chapter brings three exciting additions to Arc Raiders. There will be a new Map Condition, new Arc Threat, and the start of another Player Project.

Interestingly, we’re going to see some sort of map update during the month, but Embark didn’t share anymore details. The next Raider Deck will also deploy in February, alongside a new Expedition Window.

The Flashpoint chapter begins in March, when we’re expecting another new Map Condition, one more new Arc Threat, as well as another Player Project. March’s most interesting addition is an update to everyone’s trusty rooster friend, Scrappy.

Finally, April is when the big guns come out, because that’s when the first new map of 2026 will arrive in Arc Raiders. With it, comes a new large Arc, which is to be expected. A new Map Condition will debut then, too, likely starting off on the new map.

That’s pretty much it, but seeing as we’re just one day away from the start of the January stage, things are about to get exciting again in Arc Raiders.

#4163. Nioh 3’s generous demo is out now, and your progress carries over to the full game

If you’re looking for a way to check out one of the biggest releases of early 2026, Team Ninja has made it easy for you.

Nioh 3 is one of the most anticipated games of 2026, and it’s easily among the biggest releases of February. We’re a few days away from the start of that month, however, but we don’t have to wait until then to actually play Team Ninja’s next major release.

The previously announced demo has arrived, and it’s one any fan of action games should check out, especially if you missed the PlayStation-exclusive beta held last year.

Unlike previous tests, the Nioh 3 demo is available on PC and PS5, just like the main game. This is pretty new for the series, which has typically launched first on PlayStation before coming to PC months later.

The Nioh 3 demo includes a decent portion of content from the beginning of the game. It’s enough to show off the core duality mechanic, letting you switch between the Samurai and Ninja styles at will. It also includes a preview of the game’s open field level design, which makes it sit somewhere between full open world and the more linear level design of past Nioh games.

Feedback from the previous beta has been implemented into the demo (and full release), so you may see some familiar faces, as well as areas you visited before - assuming you played that one.

Another big reason why you might want to grab the Nioh 3 demo is that your progress in it will carry over to the full version. This includes the character creator, too, meaning you can spend all day perfecting your character without having to worry about missing out on playing the actual game.

The demo even supports online multiplayer for up to three players, in case you come to Nioh for co-op. If you complete the available content, you’ll earn an in-game bonus in the full version. This is something Team Ninja has done with past Nioh titles, of course.

This time, your reward is the Twin-Snake Helmet. Just make sure you complete the demo before February 15.

Nioh 3 is out February 6 on PC, and PlayStation 5.

#4162. Grand Theft Auto VI Will Run At 30 FPS On All Consoles, But PS5 Pro Will Feature 'Improved Clarity' And Ray-Traced Shadows

Grand Theft Auto VI launches next week on Thursday, November 19, and you can preload the game on your PlayStation 5 or Xbox Series X/S starting today, Rockstar Games has announced. The studio has also revealed what kind of visuals players can expect on their respective consoles, making clear that regardless of where you play, GTA VI targets 30 FPS gameplay.

"Grand Theft Auto VI has been fully developed from the ground up to provide the best possible experience for the current generation of consoles, targeting 30 frames per second while pushing both platforms to their absolute limits to bring the vast and rich world of Leonida to life – while maintaining the density and visual fidelity of all its environments and inhabitants," Rockstar writes in a blog post.

Rockstar Games also breaks down the different graphical settings available on PlayStation and Xbox consoles. On PS5 Pro, GTA VI will feature "improved clarity through PlayStation Spectral Super Resolution (PSSR) and ray-traced shadows only available on PlayStation 5 Pro." On PS5 and PS5 Pro, the game will include "high-fidelity haptic feedback" fully integrated into DualSense controllers and adjustable via accessibility settings, improved spatial rendering so all in-game sounds take full advantage of Tempest 3D audio, and improved load times, "making Grand Theft Auto VI play best on PlayStation 5 consoles."

On Xbox consoles, Rockstar doesn't dive into performance; instead, it focuses on Xbox Cloud Gaming on Xbox Series X/S and Xbox One consoles, noting this feature will use Xbox Series S graphics settings.

GTA VI will also fully support Remote Play on PlayStation and Xbox.

GTA VI launches November 19 on PS5 and Xbox Series X/S.

For more, check out the song "Pusher" from the game's original score, then check out the GTA VI launch trailer. After that, check out this exclusive story about how GTA VI features over 170 animal species and another about its tropical storms and hurricanes.

#4161. Quantic Dream addresses toxicity, tech bugs and tutorials for Spellcasters Chronicles closed beta 2 - here's how to get a key

Here are the start and end times for the second Spellcasters Chronicles closed beta, as well as what's new in this latest test.

Quantic Dream has opened up its upcoming fantasy MOBA for a second closed beta weekend starting from today, January 29, until 9AM UTC on Monday February 2.

The closed beta is for PC only in Europe, Asia and North America and potential players can register to join the waitlist for a key at the game’s official website or on the Spellcasters Chronicles Steam page. Players who had access to the first closed beta will automatically have access to the second, but you can sign up on both the site and Steam to increase your chances of entry.

The MOBA genre is competitive in every sense and Quantic Dream is trying to break into it with a Magic the Gathering-esque spin on the format. Players build a deck of cards before queuing into teams of 3, then face off as battling mages, summoning creatures, building fortifications and casting spells rather than choosing a Hero with unique abilities in the traditional MOBA style.

Beta content includes a new map, 6 new spells and 5 new summon creatures for your deck, as well as 3 new buildings too.

Also new for this second closed beta is an introduction and tutorial for some of the game’s finer details, as well as a text chat for strategising and much-needed player reporting system to go with it. It will also feature early versions of the Spellcaster customisation system and ranked matches.

Quantic Dream has said that this closed beta places a strong emphasis on performance, memory usage and overall gameplay stability to create a smoother experience, so with that in mind, here are the minimum and recommended PC specs:

Spellcasters Chronicles is the first ever multiplayer online game from Quantic Dream, the French studio best known for cinematic narrative games like Detroit: Become Human, Heavy Rain and Beyond: Two Souls.

#4160. 'That's An Error' - Xbox Engineer Denies 360 Games Are Being Teased For Disc To Digital

Update [Fri 13th Nov 2026, 5:45pm]: Well, unfortunately we have answer - Xbox engineer Eden Marie has confirmed over on BlueSky that the inclusion of Fable III in this image was an "error".

While the post itself is private, it reads as follows (and thanks to Pure Xbox user TheBillConiglio for alerting us to this):

"Bill: Seeing an image of a library with Fable 3 having a disc to digital badge. Error, or......"

Original Story: Yesterday, Xbox starting rolling out three new console features for Xbox Insiders to try out: rotating home backgrounds, the ability to choose which side the Xbox guide pops open on, and new ways to organise disc to digital games.

They're all cool features that we're definitely keen to play around with, but what got our attention most was the image Xbox used to show off the new disc to digital update. Particularly, the games featured with the D2D licence icon plopped in the bottom-left corner of each game tile.

Did Xbox just tease the inclusion of Xbox 360 games in the D2D programme? Well, that would be true if the image depicting Fable III is to be taken at face value. At a glance, you'd probably see the image above and think, 'great, that's awesome', but the more you look at it, the weirder it gets.

Avowed famously launched on Xbox without a physical disc. So, if the theory about Xbox 360 games joining the programme is on the money, does that mean we're getting a physical copy of Avowed too? And what about Age of Empires IV? That never received a physical release either. Then If we really want to go Enola Holmes on this image, Forza games aren't D2D compatible.

We're thinking someone at Xbox might've messed up with this image. Announcements of this magnitude shouldn't be buried in an Xbox Insider update. Xbox should be shouting about it on the front page. So, why do an Xbox 360 game and two digital-only titles have D2D icons attached to them? I could think of a lazy reason.

Only time will tell, but consider us sceptical for now. We've chalked this one up to a blunder from Xbox, although it wouldn't surprise us if Xbox 360 games did eventually join the D2D programme. And hey, it's Xbox's birthday this Sunday. Maybe there's more to this than meets the eye.

@BacklogBrad the issue isn't with converting 360 or OG XBox game discs to digital versions, the issue is that those discs don't have a unique identifier assigned to them (this started with the XBox One generation, and not all of the early XBox One games have them).

Without the UID there's no way to assign a specific disc to the digital license, meaning one disc could be used to grant anyone digital access to that game. The UID prevents this as you need to revalidate the disc licence periodically, and if you sell the disc / lend it to someone, it will validate on their device, which will invalidate your license the next time your console does an online check in.

Rockstar Games revealed last week that players can preload Grand Theft Auto VI on their console of choice the following week, and that time has arrived. The studio released a blog post today to announce that you can preload GTA VI on PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro, Xbox Series X, and Xbox Series S. If you're excited about the game, you will probably want to go ahead and do this because it will take up a whopping 212 GB of space on your drives – make the room now so you don't hit this roadblock next week when the game goes live on Thursday, November 19.

The blog post also details performance on PlayStation and Xbox consoles, and you can read more about what to expect here.

We're just over two weeks away from the launch of Grand Theft Auto VI, which recently graced the cover of Game Informer. Ahead of its November 19 launch, Rockstar Games has announced that digital preloading for GTA VI will begin next week on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S.

More specifically, preloading on Xbox Series X/S will begin Tuesday, November 10, at 12 a.m. GMT (4 p.m. PT/7 p.m. ET on November 9), and on PS5 at midnight local time in your time zone. Although Rockstar isn't producing physical discs of GTA VI, you can still buy a physical box at retail, which includes a download code for the game. The studio says, "Code-in-box versions for both consoles should be available from retailers beginning November 12."

The preload file will require 212 GB on your device, so make sure you have the space before you start the download. You can find more details about this process here.

#4158. Infinity Nikki ushers in the Year of the Horse with... a deer-themed Version 2.2

Chromatic Beings Everbright, the latest major Infinity Nikki update, has arrived, bringing Chinese New Year celebrations vibe to the game.

Infinity Nikki, the free-to-play, open-world dress-up RPG, has delivered yet another big content drop in the form of Chromatic Beings Everbright. The latest update brings the game up to version 2.2, and introduces a new narrative chapter, and gameplay taking place around a festival narrative.

If you couldn’t guess already, the new theme is Bloom Festival, inspired by Chinese New Year celebrations.

The big new story chapter takes place in the Infinity Nikki’s Wanxiang Realm. This deceptively serene and blissful region hides a dark secret, however. Chromafaces, the mythical inhabitants of the realm, have to embody fixed identities that dictate how they live and work.

These are doled out through Character Tokens, which are used to assign roles to each individual. The story follows Nikki as she uncovers the script that runs the realm and the facade it props up. Nikki will help free Chromafaces and dispel the illusion.

The Wanxiang Realm is split into three areas. Cai Ye is your typical lantern-lit district, where festivals and fireworks happen. Kongming Gorge is almost the opposite of that; a quiet and cold place. Finally, Jiuhua Pavilion literally floats above the region, and it's home to neverending music and dance.

The other big addition in 2.2 are the two new 5-Star Resonance Outfits with some interesting gameplay implications. Where Wanxiang Weaves Life is inspired by wuxia aesthetics, and true to its inspirations, it lets Nikki shapeshift into different Spirit Personas - and automatically collect resources in her vicinity.

Chroma's Mortal Heart, on the other hand, allows Nikki to fly around the Wanxiang Realm, drawing on the power of the Celestial Deer. This outfit also uses Celestial Deer Vision to automatically ping and mark treasure chests around her.

You can also look forward to Nefarious Shadows, a new Ability Outfit, which lets Nikki see through disguises, and reveals hidden paths in the world.

As with every major update, of course, there are themed activities and limited-time events throughout. Hotpot House is a cooking minigame where you attempt to run the eponymous restaurant, whereas Flavor Frenzy is series of platforming challenges that tasks you with gathering ingredients. Fortune Mahjong is a little more straightforward, with support for solo and multiplayer play.

If you’re jumping back into the game soon, be sure to hit up our Infinity Nikki codes page for some freebies.

#4156. Pokemon TCG Flowing Fists Released Early With Blastoise Revealed

Sam Woods is TheGamer’s Senior Reporter. He’s been in games journalism since 2020 and has undertaken a variety of roles in that time. These have included roles such as SEO Editor, Managing Editor at DualShockers, and Global Head of Gaming, and he's also been seen on the BBC. He was promoted to the Senior Reporter position in 2025 following a series of high-quality reports and exclusives for TheGamer.

Since 2020, Sam has written over 3,000 articles and specializes in telling the stories of the people behind the games. He’s interviewed the biggest game directors, some of the industry’s top talents, told the stories of how indie games came to be, and spoken to players about what really makes them tick. He’s also interviewed some of the world’s biggest musical artists to find out how the medium has inspired their work, and TV and Film actors about their roles in video game adaptations. He even hosted a PAX panel in 2021 and made a documentary in 2024 surrounding the creation of a Disney game.

Alongside this, Sam focuses on breaking news. He got the scoop on Perfect Dark’s cancellation, provided context on some AI drama, and revealed that Lady Dimitrescu’s actress would love to step back into the character’s giant shoes. These articles have been picked up by the biggest gaming sites, including IGN, GameSpot, and PC Gamer. He also loves to dive into the numbers behind the games.

Sam’s journey in games journalism has taken him all over the world. He’s covered Gamescom in Germany, Summer Game Fest in Los Angeles, and Tokyo Game Show in Japan, each on three occasions.

He’s been learning Japanese since 2024 with the intention of identifying and translating Japanese-language news and bringing it to English-language audiences first, something he’s done countless times.

Sam’s first review was 2020’s Battletoads reboot, and he’s since reviewed games in The Legend of Zelda, Super Mario, and Pokemon franchises.

We've only just had the release of the Pokemon Trading Card Game's most recent expansion, Delta Reign, but it seems like attention is already moving on from that set to the next, Flowing Fists.

Although Flowing Fists doesn't launch until February next year, some people on social media have begun getting their hands on products early, giving us our first look at some of the cards in the set, including a stunning Blastoise Illustration Rare.

The upcoming Flowing Fists set will pull cards from the Japanese-language expansion, Aura Seeker. As the name might suggest, the expansion will be centered around Mega Lucario Z, which was first introduced in Pokemon Legends: Z-A last year. We've had early glimpses of the Japanese Mega Lucario Z ex and Mega Garchomp ex Special Illustration Rares, and now the English versions, along with a handful of other unrevealed cards, have come to light.

It's unclear how, but some people have managed to get their hands on a bunch of single Flowing Fists blisters and are pulling what will undoubtedly be the set's most desirable cards.

As is so often the case, the images look like they've been taken on a potato, but the quality of the cards shown mean the set is going to be an exciting one.

The Mega Garchomp Z Special Illustration Rare features the Pokemon rocketing toward the camera, its two blades ready to attack. It can be seen below:

The Mega Lucario Special Illustration Rare was also pulled early, and features the new form of the Pokemon looking rather majestic. It's ability, Aura Seeker, matches the Japanese set's name.

The star of the show, though, is the Blastoise Illustration Rare. While it may have been "demoted" from Special Illustration Rare status, with the last one it received coming in the 151 set, this card is spectacular. It features one of the coolest depictions of the Pokemon standing in a rocky cavern, surrounded by water. I may be a little bit of a Gen 1 simp, but it's a great card.

Should more photos emerge throughout the day, we'll update this article, but I have a feeling Flowing Fists will be better than any standard set the Pokemon Trading Card Game received this year.

We want to hear from you. Share your perspective in the comments below, and please keep the conversation respectful.

#4155. Zenelss Zone Zero Version 2.6 has you playing as an event planner and social media manager for an idol group

Zenelss Zone Zero's Encore for an Old Dream has a good excuse for introducing some new mechanics to the action game.

Zenless Zone Zero’s latest Special Program has delivered a tonne of information about the game’s big upcoming update, Version 2.6. This latest addition kicks off celebrations in New Eridu, and it’s dubbed Encore for an Old Dream.

Version 2.6 is not far off, either, arriving in ZZZ on February 6 - exactly one week from today. Encore for an Old Dream is something of an in-between story that takes place after the end of Season 2.

The narrative of 2.6 sees the Proxies’ return to Sixth Street for New Eridu's annual Gilded Carrot Day. At the centre of the celebrations is the debut of idol group Angels of Delusion at the 404 Error music venue, but not all is as it seems.

The story follows the Proxies getting invited backstage to support the group, which also includes helping them set up practice schedules, organise events and manage social media activities. There’s a rhythm minigame as part of that, along with new maps and mechanics for Marcel Adventure.

Angels of Delusion is also the group that the two new Agents being introduced in this update belong to. Members of the same group are capable of performing coordinated attacks. The new arrivals are Sunna and Aria.

Sunna is a an S-Rank Physical Support Agent who specialises in boosting teammates using Attack and Anomaly. Her Ultimate sees her pull out a giant hammer to land heavy damage, and bring teammates into combat using Quick Assist. Sunna’s companion, Bubblegum, can cast Cat's Gaze on enemies, marking them for detonation. Bubblegum can also buff the squad’s attack.

Aria is the other new arrival, the group’s lead vocalist who can shift between two forms, idol projection and construct. Aria is an Ether Anomaly Agent who also deals high burst damage, specifically against enemies who suffer from any Attribute Anomalies.

Sunna and Aria also benefit from the support of the amusingly named Bangboo Biggest Fan, a fan club president who can heal them over time, and boost the squad’s Attack any time two or more Angels of Delusion members are present.

Version 2.6’s S-Rank re-runs are Yixuan (Auric Ink - Rupture), and Yuzuha (Physical - Support), who you can look forward to as part of the banners.

Version 2.6 will also expand Hollow Zero with a new game mode, Operation Matrix. The mode offers themed stages that rotate weekly, each offering new mechanics. You can now also Sweep in Hollow Zero.

Beyond all the celebrations, this update also brings combat kit overhauls to a couple of older S-Rank characters, Lycaon and Harumasa. You can look forward to multiple limited-time events, too, including one where you can earn a new outfit for Pan Yinhu.

The big event is naturally going to be themed around Gilded Carrot Day, and it actually starts today. There’s the usual run of login rewards (about 3,300 Polychromes), as well as daily activities. Yet another login event - Gilded Surprise, Wonderful Boo-ns - will be available February 14-23, offering daily draws from a pool of 4 billion Polychrome.

As always, there’s no reason not to catch up on the latest set of Zenless Zone Zero codes for some free in-game items.
